reusable_binding.authorization_rule: Exact content-hashed JSON only; filename must equal deterministic request identity; no symlinks or paths outside the dedicated root.
reusable_binding.journal_rule: Journal path derives from identity under /private/tmp/dev014-lifecycle-probes; no user-selected journal path.
reusable_binding.prior_attempt_rule: Existing lifecycle journals are discovered and any previously attempted request identity or mint is rejected.
reusable_binding.credential_rule: Existing BIRDEYE-only environment binding and fixed runner remain unchanged; no arbitrary command, import, URL, or credential argument.

reused_components: Existing safe BIRDEYE wrapper and fixed probe runner
Canonical Birdeye V3 request builder and binding
Existing atomic one-request journal and storage limits
Shared 15m partial-valid normalizer and observed lifecycle reducer
new_code_justification: The wrapper previously required a new source mode and hard-coded path per mint. The narrow binding accepts only an identity-named frozen authorization from one safe root and still invokes one fixed runner. It supplies reusable selection, not another provider path or launcher.

cohort_eligibility.rule: Each excluded mint retains its existing status and provenance; it cannot block independently eligible mints. A completed provider request and a qualified lifecycle observation are accounted separately.

provider_request_estimate.current_reusable_contract: One bounded 15m V3 request per exact authorization.
provider_request_estimate.cadence_floor: At most 10 historical requests per rolling 60 seconds; serialized execution implies at least 56 rolling-minute windows before runtime health and cooldown overhead.
provider_request_estimate.coverage_limit: One response establishes observed-only or partial coverage, never complete lifetime coverage by assumption.

storage_estimate.per_request: Existing compact journal/artifact <=1MiB; typical derived milestones are materially smaller but are not assumed for safety accounting.
storage_estimate.conclusion: A 551-request cohort cannot use separate worst-case 1MiB artifacts under the 100MiB ceiling. It requires an explicitly qualified compact segmented cohort persistence composition or a smaller finite batch; no such cohort executor is implemented here.

missing_cohort_execution_capability: A finite, segmented, compact cohort coordinator that serializes the already-qualified fixed runner/authorization contract while enforcing the existing 100MiB ceiling and preserving per-mint exclusion accounting. This must reuse the existing segmented journal and not be built unless separately authorized.
regression: 12 focused provider-free tests passed: reusable wrapper binding, isolated lifecycle projection, probe/no-repeat, wrapper fixture, and shared normalizer.
next_gate: Stop before acquisition. A bounded real-data validation needs a separately authorized one-request frozen authorization placed in the safe root. Cohort work additionally requires separate authority for the missing compact coordinator; do not claim readiness for 551 requests.
